content:
Ahead of Apple's special event, Bloomberg released the latest report, detailing the ten-year development journey of Apple's foldable iPhone.

The report highlights former Apple CEO Tim Cook's involvement in the project and reveals the possible price of the foldable iPhone.

Mark Gurman pointed out that Apple engineers began developing the iPhone Fold around 2016. In 2020, after returning from a business trip to China, Cook became "unusually excited" about foldable phones. He reportedly pushed Apple's hardware team to accelerate the development of the company's first foldable product.

Cook generally "does not participate in the conception of new products." Therefore, his personal involvement in the development of the foldable iPhone adds weight to the project:

As for the pricing of the foldable iPhone (which everyone inside Apple calls the iPhone Ultra), the company's original entry-level target price was US$1,999. However, recent increases in component costs have pushed this target price up to US$2,199.

Some versions with larger storage capacities may cost close to US$3,000. By comparison, the standard iPhone currently starts at US$799, while the iPhone 17 Pro starts at US$1,099.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone Ultra tomorrow. 9to5Mac will be live at the Steve Jobs Theater to bring you comprehensive in-depth coverage.
